title: Track C — Exact 2-WL Implementation and Timing-Boundary Audit

2WL_definition.tuple_space: V^2; ordered pairs generated by itertools.product(range(n), repeat=2)
2WL_definition.initial_atomic_color: Shared palette over equality pattern of tuple coordinates plus all directed Z[t[i],t[j]] relations.
2WL_definition.refinement: For each ordered pair t and each v in V, form the 2-coordinate replacement color tuple; sort the multiset over v; new feature is (old_color, sorted replacement-color tuples).
2WL_definition.palette: Shared across all structures in the compared same-n population/batch.
2WL_definition.stability: Stop when no previous color class is split by the new coloring.
2WL_definition.output_signature: Sorted counts of final colors, using the shared palette.

timing_boundary.included: 2-WL tuple construction, atomic-color construction, iterative refinement to stability, and final signatures for the supplied matched batch.
timing_boundary.excluded: Generation of the frozen posets/workload and exact nonisomorphism deduplication.
timing_boundary.batch_semantics: Historical implementation computes a shared palette across the supplied batch, so Track C timing must preserve that batch semantics rather than silently convert to per-instance independent WL calls.

implementation_decision.baseline: Preserve the exact historical batch_kwl semantics as the reference 2-WL algorithm.
implementation_decision.optimization_rule: Any optimization must be semantics-checked against this reference before timing and then frozen. No post-result tuning.
implementation_decision.reason: User requested a fair comparison against the now-optimized engine; implementation engineering is allowed, but mathematical/algorithmic 2-WL semantics may not change.

comparison_firewall: No claim that 2-WL solves the full G-to-poset reconstruction task.
No general expressive equivalence or dominance claim.
